question: In the lecture, how does the definition of continuity relate the behavior of a function near a point \(c\) to its value at \(c\), and why does the linear function \(f(x)=ax+b\) satisfy this condition at every real number?
answer: The definition states that for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists a \(\delta>0\) such that whenever \(|x-c|<\delta\) (with \(x\) in the domain), we have \(|f(x)-f(c)|<\varepsilon\). This links the function’s values arbitrarily close to \(c\) with the value at \(c\). For the linear function \(f(x)=ax+b\), the difference \(|f(x)-f(c)|=|a(x-c)|=|a|\,|x-c|\) can be made smaller than any chosen \(\varepsilon\) by taking \(\delta=\varepsilon/|a|\), so the condition holds for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}\).

question: Explain how the epsilon‑delta definition can be used to prove that \(\sin x\) is continuous at an arbitrary real point \(c\), and indicate how the boundedness of \(\sin x\) (obtained from the previous identity) is employed in the proof.
